newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Nov 8.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Nov 8.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

No decision is imminent on the fate of Conrad Black's stake in Australian newspaper group John Fairfax Holdings Ltd, the president of Black's Hollinger Inc said on Thursday night. The Australian government said Thursday it would not widen its media industry review to include foreign ownership, effectively rebuffing Black's call on Wednesday for reform of the rules so he could double his 25 percent Fairfax stake.

A promotion of a free ride on the Eurostar under-Channel rail express between London and Paris or Brussels has provoked a run on Britain's Times newspaper as readers scramble to accumulate tokens. News Corp Ltd's News International said it had increased its daily print run by between 150,000 and 180,000.

RTZ-CRA on Thursday said it wanted its Australian miners to work harder for the same wages to meet increased coal demand from Asian power stations. Predicting a six percent rise in world demand for steam coal in the next 10 years, RTZ-CRA deputy chief executive Leon Davis pointed at a discrepancy between low productivity in Australia compared with the United States.

Gulf Canada Resources Ltd said on Thursday night that it and Hardy Oil & Gas Plc had conducted due diligence to see if they could launch a higher bid for Command, the target of a A$354.5 million (C$368.7 million) bid from Cairn Energy Plc. But that they had decided Cairn's A$1.10 (C$1.14) per share offer for the company "was fully valued," which prevented a sweetened offer. Cairn Energy also announced in London overnight that SOCO International, which holds 32.6 percent of Command, had accepted its bid.
Discovery Petroleum NL said shareholders should not accept the 80 cent per share takeover bid by U.K.-based Premier Oil Plc and should wait to see if Oil Search Ltd decides to launch a rival bid.

The shares of listed Australian stock broker McIntosh Securities Ltd rose on Thursday on speculation that the company was a takeover target. Market sources said McIntosh was believed to have held talks with a number of overseas brokers in the last six months, including U.S. securities house Merrill Lynch and Co about possible partnerships or joint ventures.
